macro_context: Nightly pass during the election count; full evidence in journal/research/2026-11-03-dossier.md. Futures fell after the close as the count pointed to a Democratic sweep (Kalshi Senate D above 90% from about 75% before polls closed, House 99%) and Hinojosa, who has pledged a data-center moratorium, led Abbott for Texas governor (Texas is about 27% of US data-center capacity). IBKR at 21:44 ET: ES -1.1%, NQ -2.0%, RTY -0.7%; after hours QQQ -2.0%, SMH -2.7%, IWM -0.8%, XLV +0.2%, TLT +0.6%, even though AMD (+3.4%), ANET (+5.9%) and SMCI (+3.9%) all beat and guided up. A general index-gap base rate has no edge (n=53); the edge, such as it is, sits only in tech-led gaps after a tech up day, and only while the tech gap holds. One idea tonight: a second draft idea, long XLV / short SMH, was dropped after review because it was the same bet with more market beta (its result tracked a plain SMH short at 0.89 correlation, and XLV added nothing in the history). The main risk is a post-election relief rally that fills the tech gap (vol crush from VIX1D 22.3, open buyback windows, hedge funds already underweight AI, UBS's 'combustible setup'), as after 2016's overnight plunge; Texas early counts also tend to lean Democratic before Election Day votes are added, so the moratorium scare may fade. In-window: ADP 08:15, Treasury refunding 08:30, ISM services 10:00. After the close (after our exit): APP, QCOM, ARM earnings; election counts continue. My read: index 50/50 from the open; small caps beat the Nasdaq-100 about 60/40 if the tech gap holds.

ideas.thesis: The overnight drop is a policy repricing of megacap AI (a Democratic Senate, a Texas data-center moratorium threat), not an earnings one: AMD, ANET and SMCI beat and traded up while QQQ fell 2.0% and SMH 2.7% after hours, and the Russell held up better (RTY -0.7% vs NQ -2.0%). Small caps carry little AI exposure and gain from the lower yields a sweep brings. In our history, when a tech-led gap-down held, IWM kept beating QQQ from the open: 63% of 30 tech-led gap-downs, and 13 of 17 (10 of 13 declustered) when SMH gapped down 2% or more the day after a 1.5%+ gain, as tonight (median +67 bp, spread sd 76 bp, the steadiest form of the 'AI keeps lagging' view). Leveraged Nasdaq-100 funds trade $2.4B per 1% at the close versus $0.1B for the Russell, a small extra push if the day stays down. The edge exists only while the tech gap holds: when SMH's gap was a smaller -1% to -2%, the pair won 51% (n=35), so the stand-downs drop the idea if tech recovers much before the open.
ideas.invalidation: QQQ trades back above 685.28, Tuesday's close (gap fully filled), or the pair is down more than 0.9% from the open (about one day's spread standard deviation).
